state:
Goal `tools-server`: `tools:server/stopping-and-reloading-the-drain` has its proofs. Three features
of the group still owe, and `bun nv proofs --owed --group tools:server` lists what each owes:
`tools:server/the-server-block`, `tools:server/nvs-service` and `tools:server/nvs-serve`. Nothing is
blocked.

The drain section says what the binary does, and the binary differs from
`rule:concurrency/a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly` in two places, each a gap record: a reload
begins no drain (`data/gaps/nvs-cli/a-reload-closes-no-connection.json`), and `drain_timeout` bounds
only the wait between two requests, never a request that is running
(`data/gaps/nvs-server/drain-period-does-not-end-a-running-request.json`). A description written
for the `[server]` block or for `nvs service stop` says the same, not what the rule says.

A section passes `help` when it shows a fenced block or a table row holding code; an indented usage
block does not count (`tools/nv/proofs/roster.ts:160`). A fenced `nvs` block in this chapter is
written `nvs skip`. A `.nvst` case cannot name a mount (`crates/nvs-test/src/request.rs:67`), and a
feature of this chapter is credited by a `// covers:` marker above a Rust `#[test]` alone. An
example or an attack that needs a configuration key reads the `nvs.toml` in its own directory.

`crates/nvs-cli/tests/live_config.rs`'s `Server` ends its process with `kill`, so a case there
cannot observe a graceful stop, and what a stop does is pinned inside the crates
(`crates/nvs-cli/src/serve.rs:4031`). The goal's context gained `crates/nvs-config/src/server.rs`;
the pack printed neither `crates/nvs-cli/src/stop.rs` nor `crates/nvs-server/src/io.rs`, which the
drain slice read and the three left do not need.

next.note: One slice is one feature with all its feature proofs:

items.text: **`tools:server/the-server-block`** — owes about, examples, hostile, tests. `rule:http-server/the-server-block-is-boot-class`. The section is `docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:36`, and its line `docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:53` still gives `drain_timeout` the rule's meaning: correct it to what `# Stopping and reloading: the drain` says. `crates/nvs-config/src/server.rs:219` resolves the waits, `crates/nvs-config/src/server.rs:1076` is a case a `// covers:` marker fits, and `crates/nvs-cli/tests/live_config.rs:769` reloads the block's switches from outside.

**`tools:server/nvs-service`** — owes about, examples, help, hostile, tests. `rule:packaging/a-service-is-one-stored-argv` and `rule:packaging/the-installer-is-a-sink`. The section is `docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:406` and needs a fenced block; `crates/nvs-cli/src/service.rs:4355` is a case a marker fits.

**`tools:server/nvs-serve`** — owes about, examples, hostile, tests. `rule:security/isolate-shares-nothing`. The section is `docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:8`, and `crates/nvs-cli/tests/live_config.rs:86` starts the built `nvs serve` over a program, which a from-outside case needs.

backlog: A reload closes no connection, against `rule:concurrency/a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly` and ADR 0083 § 7 — gap record `data/gaps/nvs-cli/a-reload-closes-no-connection.json`.

The drain period does not end a running HTTP request, against the same rule — gap record `data/gaps/nvs-server/drain-period-does-not-end-a-running-request.json`; `crates/nvs-config/src/server.rs:128` and the `drain_timeout` comment in `crates/nvs-config/src/default.toml:471` describe the rule's reading.
